function: Predictive beamforming and vehicle-to-RSU assignment in a digital-twin ISAC network: two bidirectional LSTMs predict the beamforming vectors and the assignment (p. 10, p. 11).
system: Two RSUs, mmWave ULA with Nt = Nr = 32 antennas, single-antenna vehicles (MISO), 30 GHz, highway; no RIS (p. 3, p. 11, p. 12).
method: Two bidirectional LSTMs (flatten, ReLU dense layers); supervised (inferred from MSE loss and accuracy rate; labels' source not stated); 10,000 training samples (p. 10, p. 11).
data_channel: Own simulator: steering-vector model with d^-2 path loss (-70 dB at 1 m), Poisson vehicle arrivals; 10,000 training, 3,000 validation samples (p. 4, p. 11, p. 12, p. 13).
test_conditions: Trained at Nt = Nr = 32, curves per number of vehicles; tested over 10-100 vehicles, 20-40 antennas, dynamic arrivals; retraining not stated (p. 11, p. 12, p. 13).
baselines: Heuristic algorithm, greedy algorithm and distance-based matching, all non-learned; no learned baseline (p. 11).
metrics: Accuracy rate of vehicle assignment, beamforming MSE, average and total throughput (bit/symbol), throughput gain over distance-based matching, root of CRB (RCRB) (p. 11, p. 12, p. 13).
complexity: Order of complexity: LSTM O(8h1(h1+e1)); greedy and heuristic O(K^2 Nt + I K^2 Nt^2/epsilon) per iteration; no runtime numbers given (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "is the path-loss coefficient, which can be computed by" - own steering-vector channel with d^-2 path loss and fixed gains (Table I, p. 12); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "train the LSTM networks with a training set of 10,000 samples" - no statement that a model is tested at a number of vehicles, antennas or in a scenario it was not trained for.
q3_support: p. 11: "the heuristic algorithm, the LSTM-based method, the Greedy method" - heuristic, greedy and distance-based matching are all non-learned; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the total time complexity of the proposed LSTM framework can be written as" - Section VI-C gives the order of complexity of the LSTM and of the greedy and heuristic algorithms (Eq. 52-53).
q5_support: p. 11: "training set of 10,000 samples and a validation set of 3,000" - self-generated data; no link, repository or DOI for code or data anywhere in the paper.
notes: Preprint (arXiv v1) of the published paper. Included because the bidirectional LSTMs learn the beamforming and, jointly with it, the vehicle-RSU assignment, a decision above the physical layer (p. 10, p. 11). Area 5: the beamforming serves sensing and communication under a PCRB sensing constraint (p. 7, p. 8); the EKF tracking and the greedy and heuristic algorithms are not learned. q2: the paper never says that a trained model is tested at a number of vehicles or antennas, or in a scenario, that it was not trained for; Fig. 5 and 6 show training curves per number of vehicles (p. 11, p. 12) and the dynamic-arrival tests of Fig. 9 and 10 (p. 13) do not say how the LSTM was trained, so the reviewer may re-check. q4: Big-O analysis only, no measured runtime.
